examples.ko: 이번 대회의 우승자는 열두 살 아이예요.
examples.en: The winner of this contest is a twelve-year-old child.
The teacher hung a gold medal on the winner.

examples.ko: 저는 작년 우승자와 같이 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: I took a photo with last year's winner.
Nobody knows yet who the winner is.
A reporter is interviewing the marathon winner.
I learned a lot from hearing the winner's story.

explain: '우승하다'는 동사로 쓰고, '우승자'는 그 일을 한 사람이에요. 시험이나 달리기에서는 '1등'을 많이 쓰고, '우승'은 대회나 리그처럼 이름이 있는 경기에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: '우승하다' is the verb, and '우승자' is the person who did it. For exams or races people often say '1등' (first place); '우승' fits named contests and leagues.

examples.en: I do training every evening.
The training was so hard that I took a day off.

examples.ko: 새 직원 트레이닝은 이 주 동안 해요.
examples.en: The new staff training lasts two weeks.
I also want to join this training.
Training is important, but resting is important too.
I am building my stamina with training at home.

explain: 운동에는 '운동', 회사나 학교의 교육에는 '교육'을 쓰는 경우가 많아서 '트레이닝'은 조금 전문적인 느낌이 있어요. '트레이닝복', '트레이닝 바지'처럼 운동할 때 입는 옷 이름에도 나와요.
explain_en: Plain exercise is usually '운동' and workplace or school instruction is often '교육', so '트레이닝' sounds a bit specialized. It also appears in clothing names like '트레이닝복' and '트레이닝 바지'.

examples.en: That person has really good manners.
Table manners differ a little from country to country.
You have to mind your manners in public places.
Let's learn subway manners too.

examples.ko: 저는 첫인사 매너에 신경을 많이 써요.
examples.en: I pay a lot of attention to manners when greeting someone.
I judge people by their manners, not their looks.

explain: '매너가 좋다', '매너가 없다'처럼 써요. '매너'는 외래어라서 가볍게 말할 때 어울리고, '예의'는 더 정중한 한자어예요. '예의 바르다'와 '매너 좋다'처럼 같이 쓰는 말도 달라요.
explain_en: It is used as '매너가 좋다' or '매너가 없다'. '매너' is a loanword that suits casual speech, while '예의' is a more formal Sino-Korean word. They also pair with different words: '예의 바르다' versus '매너 좋다'.

examples.en: This case is still a mystery.

examples.ko: 저는 밤에 미스터리 영화를 자주 봐요.
examples.en: I often watch mystery movies at night.
Solving a mystery is really fun.
There are a lot of mysteries on that island.
The mystery usually gets revealed at the end.
Mysteries are nice, but I like comedies more.

explain: '수수께끼'는 한국어 느낌이 나는 말이고 '미스터리'는 외래어예요. 장르를 말할 때는 '미스터리 영화', '미스터리 소설'처럼 앞에 붙여 써요.
explain_en: '수수께끼' is the native Korean word and '미스터리' is a loanword. For genres, put it in front: '미스터리 영화', '미스터리 소설'.

examples.en: This baseball bat is too heavy.
The player held the bat and waited for the ball.
Bats are made of wood or metal.
The ball hit the bat and flew far away.
The child hit the ball hard with the bat.

examples.ko: 글러브뿐 아니라 배트도 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: I need to buy a new bat, not just a glove.

explain: 야구 방망이를 '방망이'라고도 하지만 야구에서는 '배트'를 더 자주 써요. 동물 박쥐는 영어로 bat이지만 한국어로는 '박쥐'라고 해요.
explain_en: A baseball bat can also be called '방망이', but in baseball '배트' is more common. The animal bat is '박쥐' in Korean, not '배트'.

examples.en: The child came running at the mother's call.
I was called by the teacher and went to the staff room.
I heard the call but pretended I didn't.
That song sounded like a call from home.
It was an urgent call, so I hurried out.
I went outside because my friend called me.

explain: '부르다'의 명사형이에요. '부름을 받다'는 격식 있는 말이고, 일상 대화에서는 '불러서 갔어요'처럼 동사로 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is the noun form of '부르다'. '부름을 받다' is formal; in everyday talk people usually use the verb, as in '불러서 갔어요'.

examples.en: There is a shovel in the garden.
My father dug the ground with a shovel.
We took shovels and cleared the snow.
Please keep the shovel in the storage room.
A lot of dirt stuck to the shovel.
I can lend you a shovel too, if you need.

explain: '삽으로 땅을 파다'처럼 '파다'와 자주 써요. 작은 화분용은 '모종삽'이라고 불러요. '삽질'은 쓸데없이 고생했다는 뜻의 속어로도 써요.

phrases.en: I wasted effort all night and have nothing to show for it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓸데없는 일에 힘만 들이고 소득이 없을 때 쓰는 속어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Slang for working hard on something that leads nowhere.

explain_en: It often goes with '파다', as in '삽으로 땅을 파다'. A small garden trowel is a '모종삽'. '삽질' is also slang for doing a lot of work for nothing.

examples.en: I shake hands with people I meet for the first time.
Yesterday I shook hands with the new boss.
I will shake hands with the guest first tomorrow.
The hand I shook was very warm.
The two smiled, shook hands, and parted.
I was really happy to shake hands with my teacher.

explain: 악수하는 상대 뒤에 '와/과'나 '하고'를 붙여서 '친구와 악수하다'처럼 써요. '악수를 하다'로 띄어 써도 같아요.
explain_en: The other person takes '와/과' or '하고', as in '친구와 악수하다'. You can also split it as '악수를 하다' with the same meaning.

examples.en: A big earthquake happened in Japan.
A big earthquake comes suddenly, at any time.
That city went through a big earthquake long ago.
We prepare water and food for a big earthquake.
Many houses collapsed in the big earthquake.
A big earthquake is scary, but a tsunami is scarier.

explain: '지진' 앞에 '대'가 붙은 말이에요. 일상에서는 '큰 지진'이라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요. 뉴스에서는 '강진'이라는 말도 나와요.
explain_en: It is '지진' with '대' (big) in front. In daily talk people often just say '큰 지진'. The news also uses '강진' (strong quake).

examples.en: Grandfather walks slowly with a cane.
Without a cane, it is hard to walk.
I left the cane standing by the door.

examples.ko: 동화 속 마법사가 지팡이로 마법을 걸었어요.
examples.en: The wizard in the fairy tale cast a spell with his staff.
Grandmother leaned on her cane and rested for a moment.
I will give my parents a cane as a gift too.

explain: '지팡이를 짚다'처럼 '짚다'와 함께 써요. 동화나 영화에서는 마법사의 지팡이도 같은 말로 불러요. 산에서 쓰는 것은 '등산 스틱'이라고 많이 해요.
explain_en: It pairs with the verb '짚다', as in '지팡이를 짚다'. A wizard's staff in stories is also a '지팡이'. The kind used on mountain hikes is often called a '등산 스틱'.

examples.en: An environmental activist came to our school.
The activist collected signatures on the street.
I interviewed a human rights activist in person.
There is time to ask that activist questions.
We picked up beach trash together with an activist.
Young activists are also increasing.

explain: '환경 활동가', '인권 활동가'처럼 앞에 분야 이름을 붙여 자주 써요. 사회 문제를 바꾸려고 움직이는 사람에게 쓰기 때문에 일반 직업 이름과는 조금 달라요.
explain_en: It usually takes a field name in front, as in '환경 활동가' and '인권 활동가'. It is for people working to change social issues, so it feels a bit different from an ordinary job title.

examples.en: Please don't touch my desk.
The child bumped the vase and it broke.
If you poke the sleeping cat, it will get angry.
My younger sibling keeps messing with my phone.
Who touched my bag?

examples.ko: 남의 물건을 건들고 가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't touch other people's things and leave.

explain: '건드리다'를 줄인 말이라서 대화에서 자주 들려요. 물건이나 몸을 살짝 만질 때도 쓰고, 상대를 일부러 자극하거나 시비를 걸 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is a shortened form of '건드리다' and is heard often in conversation. It can mean lightly touching things or the body, and also deliberately provoking someone.

examples.en: The popular search terms change every day.
It is better to keep the search term short.
What does this search term mean?
I tried putting my name in as the search term.
I found the photo with a different search term.
Just changing the search term changes the results.

explain: 포털 사이트에서 '검색어 순위'처럼 자주 보여요. '키워드'도 비슷하게 쓰지만 키워드는 글의 핵심 단어를 말할 때도 써요. '검색창에 검색어를 입력하다'가 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
explain_en: You often see it in '검색어 순위' (search ranking) on portal sites. '키워드' is used similarly, but it can also mean the key word of a text. '검색창에 검색어를 입력하다' is a common phrase.

examples.en: I always freeze leftover rice.
I bought meat and froze it right away.

examples.ko: 이 생선은 오늘 밤에 냉동할 거예요.
examples.en: I will freeze this fish tonight.
I looked up how to freeze it on the internet.
After freezing the bread, I put it in a plastic bag.
I froze the fruit and made juice out of it.

explain: '냉동'은 얼리는 것이고 '냉장'은 차갑게 두는 것이라서 서로 달라요. 냉장고의 얼리는 칸은 '냉동실', 차가운 칸은 '냉장실'이에요. '냉동식품'처럼 명사 앞에도 붙여 써요.
explain_en: '냉동' means freezing and '냉장' means keeping chilled, so they differ. In a fridge the freezer part is '냉동실' and the cool part is '냉장실'. It also attaches to nouns, as in '냉동식품'.

examples.en: I set up the chairs in advance before a meeting.
Yesterday I set up my new computer.
We will set up the stage tomorrow morning.

examples.ko: 머리를 세팅하는 데 삼십 분 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes thirty minutes to style my hair.
I set the seats and waited for the guests.
I set the alarm and woke up early.

explain: 컴퓨터 준비, 행사장 준비, 머리 모양 만들기에 모두 써요. 영어 setting에서 온 외래어라서 대화에서 많이 들리고, 글에서는 '준비하다'나 '설정하다'가 더 자연스러울 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It covers setting up a computer, preparing an event space, and styling hair. It is a loanword from English 'setting', common in speech; in writing '준비하다' or '설정하다' often sounds more natural.

examples.en: I worry about my friend, so I advise honestly.
My teacher advised me to go to bed early.
I have one thing to say as advice to my junior.
The person giving advice isn't comfortable either.
He quietly gave his advice and left.
My older brother advised me, so I started exercising.

explain: '조언'은 도움이 되는 말이고, '충고'는 잘못을 고치라는 말에 더 가까워요. 그래서 윗사람에게 '충고할게요'라고 하면 건방지게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: '조언' is helpful advice, while '충고' leans toward telling someone to correct a fault. Saying '충고할게요' to a senior can sound presumptuous.

examples.en: A debate will be held at school tomorrow.
The debate lasted for two hours.
I am preparing for the debate with a friend.
The teacher also took part in this debate.
Many opinions came up at the debate.

examples.ko: 집에서도 토론회 방송을 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can watch the debate broadcast from home as well.

explain: '토론'은 말로 의견을 주고받는 일이고, '토론회'는 그런 자리를 여는 행사예요. 선거 때 뉴스에서 '후보 토론회'라는 말이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '토론' is the exchange of opinions in speech, and '토론회' is the event held for it. In election news you often hear '후보 토론회' (candidate debate).

examples.en: A raccoon dog came out on the mountain path last night.
Raccoon dogs mostly move around at night.
I smiled at the raccoon dog in the photo.
Please don't feed the raccoon dogs.
Raccoon dogs also live in Korean mountains.
I think the raccoon dog's face is cute.

explain: 한국의 '너구리'는 영어로 raccoon dog이고, 북미의 raccoon은 '라쿤'이라고 불러요. 그래서 둘은 서로 다른 동물이에요.
explain_en: The Korean '너구리' is the raccoon dog in English, while the North American raccoon is called '라쿤'. They are different animals.

examples.en: A strange rumor is going around the company.
That rumor is not true.
I don't believe rumors easily.
Don't pay too much attention to rumors.
What started as a small rumor grew big.
Rumors also spread very fast.

explain: '소문'이 일상에서 가장 흔한 말이고, '루머'는 근거 없는 이야기라는 느낌이 더 강해요. '소문이 돌다', '루머가 돌다'처럼 '돌다'와 자주 써요.
explain_en: '소문' is the everyday word, while '루머' feels more like groundless talk. Both pair with '돌다': '소문이 돌다', '루머가 돌다'.

examples.en: The bathroom tile is cracked and water leaks.
Tiles are fairly resistant to water.

examples.ko: 집주인이 주방 벽에 타일을 새로 붙였어요.
examples.en: The landlord put new tiles on the kitchen wall.
Water splashed on the tile, so I wiped it.
We decorated the wall with white tiles.
Tiles also come in a wide variety of colors and shapes.

explain: 욕실이나 주방의 벽과 바닥에 붙이는 얇은 판이에요. '욕실 타일', '벽 타일'처럼 장소 이름과 함께 써요. 물에 강해서 물을 많이 쓰는 곳에 붙여요.
explain_en: It is a thin plate set on bathroom and kitchen walls and floors, so it combines with place names like '욕실 타일' and '벽 타일'. It resists water, so it goes in places that get wet a lot.

examples.en: My uncle put money into a fund this year.
A fund can lose part of the principal.
The bank introduced me to a new fund.
That fund went up a lot this year.
Many people save money through funds.
It is better to study funds before you start.

explain: '펀드에 가입하다', '펀드에 투자하다'처럼 써요. 은행 예금과 달리 원금이 줄 수 있어서 가입하기 전에 설명을 꼭 읽어야 해요.
explain_en: It is used as '펀드에 가입하다' or '펀드에 투자하다'. Unlike a bank deposit, the principal can shrink, so read the explanation before joining.

examples.en: I tutor a middle school student every weekend.
Last year I tutored my younger sibling in math.

examples.ko: 방학 동안 이웃집 아이에게 영어를 과외할 거예요.
examples.en: I will tutor a neighbor's child in English during vacation.
The tutor came to our house.
I tutor as a part-time job and earn pocket money.

examples.ko: 제가 과외해 준 학생의 성적이 올랐어요.
examples.en: The grades of the student I tutored went up.

explain: 선생님은 '과외를 하다', 학생은 '과외를 받다'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요. 여러 학생이 함께 듣는 '학원'과는 달리 한 명이나 적은 인원이 가르침을 받아요.
explain_en: The teacher usually says '과외를 하다' and the student says '과외를 받다'. Unlike a '학원' (cram school) with many students, private lessons are for one person or a small group.

examples.en: There are many bacteria on your hands.
Bacteria cannot be seen with the eye.
I wash my hands with soap to get rid of bacteria.
The food was contaminated with bacteria.
Cheese and yogurt are sometimes made using bacteria.
There are bacteria that are good for the body too.

explain: '세균'이라는 한자어도 같은 대상을 가리켜요. 유산균처럼 몸에 좋은 박테리아도 있어서, 나쁜 것만 말할 때는 '병균'이라고 따로 불러요.
explain_en: The Sino-Korean word '세균' points to the same thing. Some bacteria, like lactic acid bacteria, are good for the body, and the harmful ones are separately called '병균'.

examples.en: I season meat with soy sauce.
My mother seasoned the fish deliciously.
I will season the chicken this evening.
I boil water while seasoning.
Season the vegetables and mix them well.
It was marinated for a long time, so the flavor is deep.

explain: '양념'은 명사로도 많이 써요. '양념치킨', '양념장'처럼 다른 말 앞뒤에 붙기도 해요. 간을 해서 고기를 미리 재워 두는 일은 '재우다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '양념' is very often used as a noun, and attaches to other words as in '양념치킨' and '양념장'. Leaving seasoned meat to sit beforehand is also called '재우다'.

examples.en: Our class has thirty students in total.
The class was split into two this year.
The school set up a new class.
I joined the third-year class.
The atmosphere in the class is really good.

examples.ko: 우리는 옆 학급과 축구 시합을 했어요.
examples.en: We played a soccer match against the next class.

explain: 일상에서는 '반'이 훨씬 자주 나와요. '1학년 3반'처럼 말하고, '학급'은 '학급 회의', '학급 문고'처럼 학교 안의 공식적인 말에 잘 나와요.
explain_en: In daily life '반' is far more common, as in '1학년 3반'. '학급' appears in more official school phrases such as '학급 회의' and '학급 문고'.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 개그맨이 되고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling wants to become a comedian.
That comedian's expressions are really funny.
I often see comedians on TV.
Everyone laughed loudly at the comedian's joke.
My friend took a photo with a comedian.

examples.ko: 저는 그 개그맨에게 사인을 받고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to get that comedian's autograph.

explain: 여자 코미디언은 '개그우먼'이라고 해요. 영어 gag에서 온 '개그'와 man을 합친 한국식 외래어라서 영어 comedian 대신 한국에서 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: A female comedian is a '개그우먼'. It is a Korean-made loanword combining 'gag' and 'man', used in Korea in place of English 'comedian'.

examples.en: A horse carriage appears in the old painting.

examples.ko: 마차는 말 두 마리가 끌고 있어요.
examples.en: Two horses are pulling the carriage.
I rode a carriage with the kids in the park.
We loaded the carriage full of luggage.
In the old days people went to the market by carriage.
I was surprised that the carriage's wheels were big.

explain: '마차'는 말이 끄는 것이에요. 소가 끄는 수레는 '소달구지'라고 따로 불러요. 동화나 옛날 이야기, 관광지에서 주로 만날 수 있어요.
explain_en: A '마차' is pulled by horses. A cart pulled by an ox is a separate word, '소달구지'. You mostly meet it in fairy tales, old stories, and tourist spots.

examples.en: I get diarrhea when I drink cold milk.
I had diarrhea all night yesterday.
When a baby has diarrhea, we go to the hospital.
I drank a lot of water while I had diarrhea.
I had diarrhea all day and a fever too.
I ate spoiled food and had diarrhea, so it was hard.

explain: '설사를 하다'로 띄어 쓸 수도 있어요. 병원에서는 '배탈이 났어요'라고도 말하는데, 배탈은 설사뿐 아니라 배가 아픈 증상 전체에 써요.
explain_en: You can also split it as '설사를 하다'. People also say '배탈이 났어요', and '배탈' covers stomach trouble in general, not only diarrhea.

examples.en: I disinfect wounds with medicine.
Yesterday I disinfected the room thoroughly.
They will disinfect the school classrooms tomorrow.
They are disinfecting, so the smell is a bit strong.
Disinfect your hands and go inside.

examples.ko: 컵을 끓는 물에 소독해서 다시 썼어요.
examples.en: I sterilized the cup in boiling water and used it again.

explain: '청소하다'는 더러운 것을 치우는 일이고 '소독하다'는 균을 없애는 일이라서 같이 하는 경우가 많아요. '소독약', '손 소독제'처럼 다른 말과 붙여 자주 써요.
explain_en: '청소하다' is clearing away dirt and '소독하다' is killing germs, so people often do both together. It combines with other words, as in '소독약' and '손 소독제'.

examples.en: That look is a signal that he likes you.
Don't miss the signals your body sends.
A positive signal came from the company.
Signals show more clearly in actions than in words.
I react sensitively even to small signals.
I took those words as a signal of a breakup.

explain: 일상에서 신호등, 휴대폰 신호, 손짓 신호는 모두 '신호'라고 해요. '시그널'은 마음이나 분위기를 은근히 보여 주는 신호에 주로 써요.
explain_en: Traffic lights, phone signal, and hand signals are all '신호' in daily life. '시그널' is mainly used for subtle hints about feelings or mood.

examples.en: At the zoo, the crocodile opened its mouth wide.
A crocodile stays hidden in the water for a long time.
I saw a crocodile up close for the first time.
It is dangerous to go near a crocodile.
A crocodile's teeth are very sharp.
Crocodiles also lay eggs and raise their young.

explain: 영어의 crocodile과 alligator를 한국어에서는 보통 둘 다 '악어'라고 불러요. '악어가죽 가방'처럼 가죽 이름으로도 써요.

phrases.en: That apology is nothing but crocodile tears.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속으로는 슬프지 않으면서 겉으로만 우는 척할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone only pretends to cry or feel sorry without really meaning it.

explain_en: Korean usually calls both the English 'crocodile' and 'alligator' '악어'. It also names the leather, as in '악어가죽 가방'.

examples.en: The new movie's trailer came out today.
The trailer is only two minutes long.
I watched the trailer together with a friend.
My favorite actor appears in the trailer.
Even the trailer is fun, so I look forward to the movie.
The music in the trailer was really cool.

explain: 드라마의 다음 회 안내는 '다음 회 예고'라고 하는 경우가 많아요. 영화에는 '예고편'을 써요. 둘 다 짧은 영상이에요.
explain_en: For a drama's next episode people often say '다음 회 예고', while '예고편' is used for movies. Both are short videos.

examples.en: Early-morning movies have cheaper tickets.
I watched a movie at the early showing on the weekend.
I like the early showing because there are few people.
Shall we go to the early showing tomorrow morning?
My friend likes the early showing too.
The early showing is the most comfortable for me.

explain: '조조할인'이라는 말로 아주 자주 나와요. 일반적인 시간 표현이라기보다 영화관에서 쓰는 말에 가까워요. 영화와 상관없이 이른 시간은 '이른 아침'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It shows up most often in '조조할인' (early-bird discount). It is more of a movie-theater word than a general time expression. An early morning in general is '이른 아침'.

en: leave out; skip; forget to include

examples.en: I often skip my homework.
I forgot to write my name on the test paper.
I have no plans to skip class.
I want to fix my habit of skipping medicine.
I skipped the explanation and solved the problem right away.
I left out one line, so points were deducted.

explain: 일부러 안 할 때도, 깜빡해서 못 할 때도 써요. 중립적으로 말하면 '빠뜨리다'가 무난하고, '빼먹다'는 말투가 편해요. 수업, 숙제, 식사 같은 말과 자주 어울려요.
explain_en: It covers both skipping on purpose and missing something by accident. The neutral choice is '빠뜨리다'; '빼먹다' is more casual. It often goes with class, homework, and meals.

examples.en: Our school's student council is preparing the festival.

examples.ko: 학생회는 한 달에 한 번 회의를 해요.
examples.en: The student council has a meeting once a month.
My friend is leading the student council this year.
I will join the student council next year too.
A new president of the student council was elected.
The student council and the teachers discussed it together.

explain: 중고등학교에서는 '학생회', 대학교에서는 '총학생회'를 많이 써요. 반 안의 일은 '반장'이 맡고, 학교 전체를 대표하는 사람은 '학생회장'이에요.
explain_en: Middle and high schools say '학생회', and universities often say '총학생회'. Matters inside a class are handled by the '반장' (class president), while the head of the whole school is the '학생회장'.

examples.en: The United States has a vice president as well as a president.
The vice president works to assist the president.
The people elected a new vice president.
The vice president's speech was shown on TV.
On the news, the vice president held a press conference.
A reporter asked the vice president a question.

explain: 지금 한국에는 부통령이 없어요. 대신 '국무총리'라는 자리가 있어요. 그래서 이 말은 미국 같은 다른 나라 뉴스에서 주로 나와요.
explain_en: Korea currently has no vice president. It has a '국무총리' (prime minister) instead. So this word mostly appears in news about other countries such as the U.S.

examples.en: I sent New Year greetings by text.
I will definitely start exercising in the new year.
The family gathered together to welcome the new year.

examples.ko: 신년의 첫날에는 가족과 함께 떡국을 먹어요.
examples.en: On the first day of the new year, we eat tteokguk with the family.
At the new year gathering, the boss gave a greeting.
When the new year comes, we make wishes.

explain: 신년 인사로는 '새해 복 많이 받으세요'라고 해요. '신년'은 한자어라서 격식 있는 글이나 방송에 잘 나오고, 대화에서는 '새해'를 더 많이 써요. '신년사', '신년회'처럼 붙여서도 써요.
explain_en: The greeting is '새해 복 많이 받으세요'. '신년' is Sino-Korean, so it fits formal writing and broadcasts; in conversation '새해' is more common. It also attaches to words like '신년사' and '신년회'.

examples.en: My uncle works as a programmer at a big company.
The programmer made a new app.
I have dreamed of being a programmer since I was young.
Programmers often work at night.
The programmer's desk is full of coffee.
The programmer and the designer hold a meeting together.

explain: 회사에서는 '개발자'라는 말도 자주 써요. 두 말을 거의 같은 사람에게 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 직업을 말할 때는 '프로그래머로 일하다'처럼 '로'를 붙여요.
explain_en: Companies also use the word '개발자' (developer), and the two often refer to the same people. When naming the job, add '로', as in '프로그래머로 일하다'.

examples.en: A long hose is lying in the garden.

examples.ko: 호스는 쓰고 나서 잘 감아 두세요.
examples.en: Please coil the hose neatly after using it.
Dad holds a hose and washes the car.
There is a hole in the hose, so water leaks.
I watered the flowerpots with a hose.
I pressed the end of the hose with my hand.

explain: '소방 호스', '고무 호스'처럼 앞에 종류를 붙여 써요. 딱딱한 금속이나 플라스틱 관은 '파이프'라고 해서 부드러운 '호스'와 구분해요.
explain_en: A type goes in front, as in '소방 호스' and '고무 호스'. Rigid metal or plastic tubes are called '파이프', which separates them from a flexible '호스'.

examples.en: The lipstick I just bought is really pretty.
I want to buy a red lipstick.
I always keep a lipstick in my bag.
A lipstick mark was left on the cup.
My younger sister wrote on the mirror with lipstick.

examples.ko: 저는 립스틱도 잘 안 바르는 편이에요.
examples.en: I rarely put on lipstick either.

explain: '립스틱을 바르다', '립스틱이 묻다'처럼 써요. 입술에 바르는 다른 제품으로 '립밤', '립글로스'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is used as '립스틱을 바르다' (apply) and '립스틱이 묻다' (get smeared). Other lip products include '립밤' and '립글로스'.

examples.en: My younger sibling is still innocent.
I was innocent when I was young too.
You don't need to be that naive.
With an innocent face, he believed the lie as it was.
He is innocent and kind-hearted.
Being so naive, it is easy to get cheated.

explain: 좋은 뜻으로 '때 묻지 않았다'고 칭찬할 수도 있고, 세상 물정을 모른다는 나쁜 뜻으로도 써요. 어른에게 '순진하시네요'라고 하면 놀리는 말처럼 들릴 수 있어요. '순수하다'는 거의 칭찬이에요.
explain_en: It can be a compliment meaning unspoiled, or a criticism meaning ignorant of the world. Telling an adult '순진하시네요' can sound like teasing. '순수하다' is almost always praise.

examples.en: This box is useless now.
That book was useless to me.
It seems useless, but let's take it anyway.
I threw away a lot of useless things.
This key is old, useless, and heavy.
The old information was useless, so I deleted it.

explain: 사람에게 '쓸모없다'라고 하면 아주 심한 말이 돼요. 반대말은 '쓸모 있다'이고, '쓸모가 없다'로 띄어 말하기도 해요. '필요 없다'는 지금 필요하지 않다는 느낌이고, '쓸모없다'는 쓰임이 아예 없다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Saying '쓸모없다' about a person is very harsh. The opposite is '쓸모 있다', and you can split it as '쓸모가 없다'. '필요 없다' means not needed right now, while '쓸모없다' means having no use at all.

examples.en: This piano sheet music is too difficult.
I practice a song while looking at the sheet music.
You can buy sheet music at a bookstore.
I marked the score with a pencil.
I'm a beginner who can't even read sheet music.

examples.ko: 악보의 첫 줄이 이해가 안 돼요.
examples.en: I don't understand the first line of the score.

explain: '악보를 보다', '악보를 읽다'처럼 써요. 책으로 묶은 것은 '악보집'이라고 해요. 노래 가사만 적은 종이는 악보가 아니라 '가사'예요.
explain_en: It is used as '악보를 보다' or '악보를 읽다'. A bound collection is a '악보집'. A sheet with only the lyrics is '가사', not '악보'.

examples.en: If you go to the Arctic, you can see the aurora.

examples.ko: 저는 오로라를 보러 아이슬란드에 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to go to Iceland to see the aurora.
The aurora glows green in the night sky.
I watched a video about the aurora.
The aurora also shows well only when there are no clouds.
The shape of the aurora differs every time.

explain: 한국에서는 보기 어려워서 주로 영화나 여행 이야기에서 듣게 돼요. 같은 현상을 '북극광'이라고도 하지만 일상에서는 '오로라'라고 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is hard to see in Korea, so you mostly hear it in movies and travel talk. The same phenomenon is also called '북극광', but people more often say '오로라'.

examples.en: A cheetah runs very fast.
Cheetahs live on the African grassland.
I saw a cheetah for the first time at the zoo.
The rabbit ran away from the cheetah.
Even a cheetah gets tired if it runs for long.
A cheetah's legs are long and slender.

explain: '빠르다'와 함께 자주 나와서 '치타처럼 빠르다'라고 비유로도 말해요. 비슷하게 생긴 '표범'과는 다른 동물이에요.
explain_en: It often appears with '빠르다', so '치타처럼 빠르다' works as a comparison. The similar-looking '표범' (leopard) is a different animal.

examples.en: The online mall has a lot of categories.
Please choose a category first.
Which category is this book in?
It's easier if you organize things by category.
The categories are in the top menu.
I tried dividing the items into categories.

explain: 온라인 쇼핑이나 앱에서 많이 써요. 일반 대화에서는 '종류'나 '분류'가 더 쉬운 말이에요. '분야'는 일이나 공부의 영역을 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It is common in online shopping and apps. In general conversation '종류' or '분류' are easier words. '분야' is used for a field of work or study.
